Action.description:
A pre- or post-action on a node.

The built-in tts_say and end_conversation types take no handler. The
built-in function type requires one: the handler runs inline in the
pipeline, queued behind the bot's turn. A custom type may name a handler
too, which then runs immediately when the node's actions execute; a
custom type without one must be registered in code with
FlowManager.RegisterAction. Any additional keys pass through to the
handler. The text of a tts_say action may contain {{ key }}
placeholders; see FlowConfig.

Parameters:
    type: Action type identifier.
    handler: Name of the handler in the handlers a Flow is built with.
        Required for function, optional for custom types, not allowed
        on tts_say or end_conversation.
Action.title: Action

Branch.description:
A transition chosen by a field of the tool's result.

Parameters:
    field: Key of the tool's result whose value selects the case.
    cases: Result value to node name. Keys may be written as strings,
        booleans, or numbers; they match the result value by its
        canonical string, so true: matches a result of true.
    default: Node to transition to when the value matches no case.
        When omitted, an unmatched value stays on the current node.
Branch.title: Branch

Function.description:
A tool offered at a node.

Ordinarily the entry names a NodeFunction in the handlers a Flow is
built with, and the tool's description and parameters come from that
function. A transition_only entry is defined entirely here instead: it
takes no parameters, runs no code, and moves the conversation to
transition_to when the LLM calls it.

Parameters:
    name: The tool's name, as the LLM sees it. For an ordinary entry,
        also the name of the NodeFunction in the handlers.
    transition_only: Whether the tool is defined here rather than in
        code. Requires description and a transition_to that names a
        node.
    description: What the tool is for, for the LLM. Only a
        transition_only entry has one; a NodeFunction carries its own.
    transition_to: Node to transition to after the tool completes, or
        a Branch. Omitted for tools that stay on the current node.
        Inside a subflow a target may also be return; see "Subflows"
        in FlowConfig.
    metadata: JSON data the application attaches to the tool. See
        "Metadata" in FlowConfig.
Function.title: Function

Message.description:
One message in a node's task_messages.

Parameters:
    role: Message role, e.g. developer or system.
    content: Message text. May contain {{ key }} placeholders; see
        FlowConfig.
Message.title: Message

Node.description:
One node of the flow.

A node either prompts the LLM, with task_messages and the fields that
go with them, or runs a subflow, with flow and return_to in their
place. See "Subflows" in FlowConfig.

Parameters:
    task_messages: What the LLM should do at this node. Required
        unless the node runs a subflow.
    role_message: The bot's role or personality, sent as the LLM's
        system instruction on entering this node. It persists across
        transitions until another node sets its own. May contain
        {{ key }} placeholders; see FlowConfig.
    functions: Tools offered at this node, in addition to the
        config's global_functions.
    pre_actions: Actions run before the LLM responds at this node.
    post_actions: Actions run after the LLM responds at this node.
    context_strategy: How the LLM context is updated on entering this
        node. Defaults to the FlowManager's strategy.
    respond_immediately: Whether the LLM responds as soon as the node
        is entered. Defaults to true.
    metadata: JSON data the application attaches to the node. See
        "Metadata" in FlowConfig.
    flow: Id of the subflow this node runs, a key of the config's
        flows. A node that runs a subflow takes only return_to and
        metadata besides.
    return_to: The node that return in the subflow leads to. May be
        omitted when the subflow never returns.
Node.title: Node

Subflow.description:
A set of nodes that a flow's nodes can run.

Inside a subflow a function transitions to one of the subflow's own
nodes, or to return. See "Subflows" in FlowConfig.

Parameters:
    initial_node: Name of the node the subflow starts in.
    nodes: The subflow's nodes, keyed by name.
Subflow.title: Subflow

description:
A conversation flow described as data.

Load one with FlowConfigFromFile for a YAML or JSON file,
FlowConfigFromYAML for YAML text, FlowConfigFromJSON for JSON text, or
FlowConfigFromMap for a document that is already parsed.

!include resolves paths on the application's file system and can read
any file the process can read, so it belongs only in configs the
application ships. Load a config from another source, such as a request
body, with FlowConfigFromYAML and no base directory, which rejects
!include, or with FlowConfigFromJSON.

Prompt text may refer to the manager's state with {{ key }}
placeholders: a node's role_message, the content of its task_messages,
and the text of a tts_say action. The FlowManager fills them from its
state each time it enters the node, so a value stored by a handler
earlier in the conversation can appear in a later prompt.
{{ order.size }} walks into a stored map. A key that is not in state is
an error when the node is entered. To show the LLM a literal {{ key }},
escape it as \{{ key }}.

Metadata: a node and a function each take an optional metadata mapping
of JSON values, for whatever the application wants to keep with them,
such as the id of the element a node stands for in an editor. The flow
carries it and never acts on it, and it is never sent to the LLM. A
Flow copies it onto the nodes and functions it builds, and the
FlowManager passes it to node-entered handlers and to an RTVI client as
the flow moves. Metadata is sent to the client, so keep anything the
end user should not see out of it.

Subflows: a set of nodes used by several flows, or several times in
one, is written once as a subflow under flows. A node runs it by naming
it as its flow, in place of prompts and functions of its own, and says
where the subflow's return leads:

    initial_node: verify_caller
    flows:
      verification: !include verification.yaml
    nodes:
      verify_caller:
        flow: verification
        return_to: book
      book:
        ...

Entering such a node enters the subflow at its first node. Inside a
subflow a transition target names one of its own nodes, or is return,
which leads to the return_to of the node running it; to return to two
places, run the subflow from two nodes. return_to may be omitted for a
subflow that never returns. A Flow builds a subflow's nodes once for
each node that runs it, named <node>.<subflow node>, so everything
before the dot is the node that runs the subflow; that is the name the
FlowManager reports as its current node, and the node-entered event
gives the running node separately as its parent. A config that has
subflows therefore cannot have a dot in a node name. A subflow's nodes
cannot run subflows, and global_functions are offered at them too.

Parameters:
    initial_node: Name of the node the flow starts in.
    nodes: The flow's nodes, keyed by name.
    global_functions: Tools offered at every node.
    flows: Subflows the flow's nodes can run, keyed by flow id.
title: FlowConfig
